$comment: THE ENGINE'S IDENTITY, IN ONE FILE.
Everything here is what makes this installation RTFCLMGZN rather than some
other publication built on the same machinery. Nothing here is content, and
nothing here is logic. If a value is in this file, no source file is allowed
to hardcode it a second time — newsroom/quality/site_guard.py::
check_engine_config fails the build when one does.
WHY THIS EXISTS (2026-08-15). A full audit found this publication's identity
spread across roughly 500 places: 4 separate SITE constants that each
redeclared the domain, a wordmark hand-inlined in 3 files, a desk list
written out 5 times (two of the copies had drifted apart on colour), 12
email literals, and a model price table duplicated in 2 files that disagreed
with itself. None of that is hard to fix. All of it is impossible to fix
RELIABLY without one file that owns the answer, because the fifth copy is
always the one nobody remembers.
STANDING UP A SECOND SITE: change this file, replace web/assets/brand/*,
empty web/data/* of content, run the guard. What the guard still complains
about is what is still hardcoded, and that list is the honest measure of how
close this is to being a product.
NOT HERE, ON PURPOSE: secrets and credentials. Every key lives in the
Cloudflare or GitHub environment of the account that owns the site, never in
the repository. This repo is public.

$comment_prefix: The DOM, storage and cookie namespace. Changing it is a breaking change:
it is the contract between web/data/*.js, app.js and the Python checks,
so a clone should keep 'RTFC' unless it is also regenerating every store.

$comment_subject: The BEAT. This is the honest boundary of what configuration can do. The
Scoreboard, the Grid, the Dictionary, Labs and Extensions are not generic
pages that happen to contain AI rows — their schemas presuppose models,
datacenters and vendors. A publication about a different subject reuses the
pipeline, the checks, the router, the reader and the magazine, and replaces
these five surfaces. Say that out loud in the product rather than implying
a rebrand is a config change.

$comment_short: The beat in headline register. `domain` is the long form for the writing
agents; this is the two-word version the reader sees in nav and headings.
For RTFCLMGZN it is 'AI', which is why this change leaves the live site
byte-identical to what it rendered before.

$comment_surfaces: Switches for the subject-bound surfaces. Keys must equal subject.surfaces_bound_to_subject.

$comment: The five surfaces whose SCHEMAS presuppose the AI beat (see subject.surfaces_bound_to_subject).
Each has an on/off switch and the label the reader sees. gen_engine_js stamps the switch into
index.html (footer links), gen_sitemap drops disabled URLs, functions/[[path]].js answers 404
for a disabled route, and app.js hides the hub tile, palette entry and route. RTFCLMGZN keeps
all five on; a generated niche starts with all five off until a surface pack exists for it.

$comment_desks: ONE desk list. It was previously written out five times — personas.js,
SECTION_COLORS, GLYPHS, the apply-type map and a runbook one-liner — and
two of those copies had drifted to different hex values for Frontier,
Policy and Health, so a story's colour depended on which surface drew it.

commerce.$comment: Stripe price IDs stay in the environment. Only the figures the SITE displays live here, so the page and the checkout can never quote different numbers.

cadence.$comment: Descriptive, and the source for any figure printed on the site. The cron expressions in .github/workflows are the operative schedule; these must agree with them, and check_engine_config verifies it.
cadence.$comment_ledger: From this moment the harness (log_usage.py, in the workflow) is the ONLY writer of usage rows: it measures the finished run's transcript and stamps the row with the run id. Agents write their one-sentence summary to $RTFC_RUN_SUMMARY and never touch the ledger. Any unmetered row dated after this is a harness failure and the guard says so; any row without a run tag after this was hand-written and the guard removes it.
